questions.learningObjective: evaluate raster file formats in a design critique
questions.stem: On Raster file formats: a designer reviewing a museum exhibition poster notices that a designer needs a lossless format with transparency for a logo. Which common format capability fits this need best?

options.text: A format that always averages pixels into a lossy grid
options.misconception: describes a lossy photographic format rather than the needed one

options.text: A format intended only for storing animated audio tracks
options.misconception: names a completely unrelated kind of medium

options.text: A format that can store only black and white pixels
options.misconception: invents a limitation that the common formats do not have

options.text: A format supporting lossless compression and an alpha channel

questions.explanation: For a logo needing crisp edges and transparency, a lossless format with an alpha channel preserves detail and allows a transparent background. Lossy photographic formats discard data and generally lack the transparency control required here.
questions.hint: Which two capabilities does the logo require from its chosen file format?
